title: Four ways to keep a diary

data.source: Presentism, the growing block (Broad 1923), the moving spotlight and the static block, written as four engines for one seeded R4 rotor of 6,000 steps. Twenty runs.

prediction: One CRR loop run as a presentist world, a growing block, a moving spotlight and a static block gives an observer inside it exactly the same record, with and without interventions. Only the storage differs. Whether the past acts on the present depends on the seed rule, not on which view of time is true.
baseline: The four standard views of time (McTaggart 1908; Broad 1923; Prior 1967), with the static block as the reference and the presentist engine as decoy.
why: Not every prediction held: P5_the_rule_not_the_ontology. Phoenix marks the growing block ONTOLOGY and records the comparison NOT DECIDABLE; this room re-shows it and adds presentism and the spotlight. Shared by all four: every observable. Left over: where the numbers are kept. It would become testable only with a prediction that an open future makes and a settled one does not; Phoenix says none has been written.

forks.unforeseeable outside interventions: the pre-computed engines must be rebuilt; a fact about simulating, not an observation

weighs: Every outcome is equally likely under all four views, by construction.
result: The four engines gave the inside observer one and the same record of 37 occasions (1 distinct hash), and one and the same record after a kick. At the end the presentist engine held 6 numbers, the growing block 36000, the spotlight and the static block 36000 each; the last two held all 36000 from the first moment. With the literal seed rule a presentist has to carry 37 past marks in its present state, against 1 with the closure. My first edit of the record was set for an occasion the run never reached, so that prediction is scored as missed. In the follow-up, editing the record changed 8 later seeds under the literal rule and 0 under the closure, identically in every engine. Of 5 candidate observables, 0 differed. The gaps had a lag-one correlation of -0.1352 in all four.

framework.name: Presentism, the growing block and the moving spotlight

precise_core: The logic of tenses is exact mathematics. The theses about what exists are stated in prose.
proved_by_others: Temporal logic has a broad community of logicians and computer scientists.
differing_prediction: None. Phoenix says of the growing block: "difficult direct empirical discrimination".
tested: Never; there is nothing to test.
literature: A very large philosophical literature since 1908.
engineering: A descendant only: temporal logic, which grew from the logic of tenses, is used to verify chips and software. The ontology is used for nothing.
admits_open_problems: The standard objections (how do you know it is now; the clash with relativity) are part of the literature itself.

precise_core: R1 to R6 are written exactly, with status keys. The parts are free choices: no universal q, ruler, dynamics or memory kernel (Phoenix: OPEN).
proved_by_others: Nobody outside the owner's programme. Phoenix says its own audit is not independent. Tonight's re-checks were made by model workers, not by independent people.
differing_prediction: Only through added bridges (the change clock, the regeneration law). Phoenix: the core has not yet issued a prediction.
tested: The bridges were frozen and scored on held-out real data inside the programme. No outside group has tested anything.
passed: Phoenix: no held-out CRR-specific pass; its result ledger is empty. Tonight's library ledger has no fits.
replicated: None. The one inherited first-level pass did not replicate (Phoenix).
literature: No peer-reviewed paper on CRR is cited anywhere in Phoenix, and none is known to this check.
engineering: Engineering candidates and good-practice rules only. Phoenix grades the method they rest on as known prior art.
admits_open_problems: An OPEN list in the core itself, failures kept on the ledger, and written exit conditions.

status.note: Scores are 0 to 3 on the stated scale. A line marked from_memory was not checked against a source tonight. The total is a count of ticks, not a ranking of truth.
